name.description: Optional human-readable name (used in logs and error messages).

vars.description:
Optional shared constants. Resolvable as `${vars.key}` anywhere in
the config (including inside named templates). Resolved at load time,
after env/file/secret substitution.

params.description:
Optional typed run parameters (#444) — the config's trigger-time
override surface. Each entry declares a name, scalar `type`,
`required`/`default`, a `secret` flag, and a `description`; values are
referenced as `${param.NAME}` and bound before parsing by
[`crate::params::bind`] (from `--param`, `faucet template run`, or
`POST /v1/templates/{id}/runs`). Because binding happens pre-parse, no
`${param.*}` token ever reaches a connector. See `faucet schema params`.

auth.description:
Optional named auth providers. Each entry is a `{ type, config }` spec
(the same shape as inline auth) built once and shared across every
connector that references it via `auth: { ref: <name> }`. Values are kept
as raw JSON so `faucet-auth` owns the per-type schema.

pipeline.description: Base pipeline — every matrix row is deep-merged into this.

matrix.description:
Matrix of per-row overrides. Empty or omitted means "one anonymous row"
(full pipeline runs once with no merge).

selection.description:
Optional matrix-row selection policy (#377). Currently carries only
`include_parents` — how a selected row's `parent:` / `depends_on:`
ancestors are resolved when they are not independently in the run set.
Absent = the built-in default (`include_parents: off`, strict).

delivery.description:
Delivery guarantee for every row (overridable per matrix row). Default
`at_least_once` — no behaviour change for existing configs. `exactly_once`
requires an idempotent sink, a deterministic-replay source, and a state
store (enforced at expand time).

resilience.description:
Optional resilience policy (retry / backoff / circuit-breaker /
poison-pill). Top-level in v1 (not per-matrix-row). Absent = no behaviour
change. Consumed by `faucet run`/`schedule`/`replicate`.

sla.description:
Optional data-freshness & volume SLA (#202). Top-level in v1 (not
per-matrix-row, like `resilience:`). Evaluated after every root
invocation by `faucet run`/`schedule`/`serve`/`replicate`; violations
emit metrics + warnings and never fail the run. Staleness/volume checks
require a `state:` block (enforced at expand time).

shard.description:
Optional source-shard distribution for clustered (Mode B) execution.
Only consumed by `faucet serve --cluster`: a run whose source
[is shardable](faucet_core::Source::is_shardable) is split into
`shard.count` shards processed concurrently across cluster workers.
Ignored by `faucet run` and by a non-cluster `serve`, so it is fully
backward compatible.

replication.description:
Optional snapshot→CDC replication block. Consumed only by
`faucet replicate`; ignored by `faucet run` (like `schedule:`).

backfill.description:
Optional backfill defaults (window/concurrency/timezone, #282).
Consumed only by `faucet backfill`; ignored by `faucet run` (like
`schedule:` / `replication:`). See `faucet schema backfill`.

partition.description:
Default range partitioning applied to every root row that does not
declare its own (#479). Unlike `backfill:` / `schedule:`, this IS
consumed by `faucet run` — a partitioned row fans out on every run.

schedule.description:
Optional cron schedule. Only consumed by `faucet schedule`; ignored by
`faucet run`. Presence makes the config runnable on a schedule.

lineage.description: Optional OpenLineage emission. Consumed by `faucet run`/`schedule`/`serve`.

catalog.description:
Optional Data Movement Catalog store (#279): where `faucet run` /
`schedule` / `replicate` accumulate the cross-run dataset catalog
(identity, schema timeline, volume/freshness, lineage edges). `faucet
serve` ignores this block and records into its `--history` backend.
Recording never fails a run. See `faucet schema catalog`.

notifications.description:
Optional notification / incident-routing rules (#280). Fan pipeline
lifecycle and health events (run failure/success, SLA breach, circuit
open, contract abort, DLQ threshold, scheduler stuck) out to Slack /
PagerDuty / a signed webhook. Consumed by every runtime
(`run`/`schedule`/`serve`/`replicate`); delivery never fails a run.

reconcile.description:
Optional completeness reconciliation (#502): after a successful root run,
compare rows written against an authoritative count probe and **fail the
run** on a shortfall beyond tolerance — a silent-truncation guard,
especially for `write_mode: overwrite`.

metadata_columns.description:
Optional `_faucet_*` run/lineage metadata columns (#510) stamped onto
every row by a connector-agnostic sink decorator (works for any sink).
Off unless present.

local_outputs.description:
Optional retention policy for the **local files** this pipeline's sinks
write (#587): how long they are kept before the GC reclaims them, and
whether faucet records them at all. Without the block, outputs are
tracked and inherit the runtime's default window (7 days). Recording
needs a store — `faucet serve`'s `--history`, or the `catalog:` block for
the one-shot runtimes — and is inert (with a warning) without one.
See `faucet schema local-outputs`.

type.description:
Value type. Governs coercion of the supplied value and the type
substituted when `${param.NAME}` is a config value's *entire* text.

required.description:
When true the caller MUST supply a value; there is no fallback.
Mutually exclusive with `default` (a defaulted param is by definition
optional).

default.description:
Value used when the caller supplies none. Resolved like any other config
scalar first, so `default: "${env:SINCE}"` works.

secret.description:
Marks the value as sensitive: it is registered with the redaction
registry the moment it is bound, so it never reaches logs, error
strings, API responses, or the audit log in clear.

description.description:
Human-readable purpose, surfaced by `faucet template list/show`, the
MCP `get_template` tool, and `GET /v1/templates/{id}`.

computed.description:
A **derived** value: this param is not user-supplied but computed from
other params via an interpolation expression — `${param.NAME}` and the
`${map:NAME|case=value|*=default}` lookup — resolved *after* the ordinary
params bind (#573). A computed param is excluded from the trigger surface
(supplying a value for it is an error) and is mutually exclusive with
`required`, `default`, and `secret`. Example:
`accounts_domain: { computed: "${map:region|ca=zohocloud|*=zoho}" }`.

ParamType.description:
The scalar type a param carries. Params are deliberately scalar-only: a
param substitutes into a config *value* position, and structured overrides
are what named templates / matrix rows are for.

PipelineSpec.description:
The base pipeline definition. Each matrix row is resolved against the
template catalogs below; the singular `source` / `sink` fields are the
legacy way to declare a single template (internally named `default`).

quality.description: Data-quality checks (pipeline-level; no matrix-row override in v1).

contract.description:
Data contract (pipeline-level; no matrix-row override in v1): a
versioned output schema/constraint promise enforced per page after
transforms and quality checks (#204). See `faucet schema contract`.

masking.description:
PII detection + column-level masking policy (pipeline-level; no
matrix-row override in v1): classify sensitive fields (by name pattern,
value detector, or explicit list) and redact/hash/tokenize/partial-mask
them per page — before every sink write, the DLQ, and lineage sampling
(#206). Rules can be scoped per destination sink via `applies_to`. See
`faucet schema masking` and `faucet masking`.

schema.description: Schema-drift handling policy (pipeline-level; no matrix-row override in v1).

nodes.description:
Topology-mode nodes (issue #71): an explicit graph of typed nodes
(`source` / `transform` / `tee` / `merge` / `join` / `sink`) keyed by
node id. When non-empty this pipeline runs in **topology mode** and the
top-level `matrix:` block must be empty (they are mutually exclusive).

edges.description:
Topology-mode edges connecting `nodes` (issue #71). Each edge names a
producer (`from`) and consumer (`to`); a join's incoming edges also
carry an `as:` label matching the join's `build`/`probe` edge names.

ConnectorSpec.description:
A `{ type, config }` block, the universal shape for both sources and sinks.

Source templates may additionally carry `transforms:` and
`inherit_transforms:`. Both are rejected on sink templates at expand time.

type.description:
Connector type — matches the suffix of the underlying crate
(e.g. `rest` for `faucet-source-rest`).

config.description:
Connector-specific config object. Passed through verbatim to the
connector's `serde::Deserialize` impl.

transforms.description:
Transforms bound to this source template. Applied after `T_pipeline`
and before `T_row` for every matrix row that resolves to this template.
Rejected at expand time when this `ConnectorSpec` is used as a sink.

inherit_transforms.description:
When `false`, drops upstream `T_pipeline` transforms for every matrix
row that resolves to this source template. Default `true`. Rejected
at expand time on sinks.

status.description:
Readiness ladder for the *source* side of a row (#371). Governs whether
a row runs by default. Deep-merges from template → row `source` override
like any scalar. `None` resolves to the built-in default (`active`).
Meaningful only on source templates; ignored on sinks.

tags.description:
Free-form classification tags for the *source* template (#376).
Union-merged (not replaced) with a matrix row's own `tags:` to form the
row's effective tag set. Meaningful only on source templates; ignored on
sinks. Validated at expand time (charset `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$`).

complete_for.description:
**Completeness claim** for scoped cleanup (#478). Meaningful only on
source templates; rejected at expand time on sinks — only a source knows
whether a fetch returned every record for a scope.

type.description:
Built-in transform identifier. One of: `flatten`, `rename_keys`,
`snake_case`, `select`, `drop`, `set`, `rename_field`, `cast`, `redact`,
`value_case`. See the docs-site cookbook page on transforms for
per-transform config schemas.

config.description: Transform-specific config object (e.g. `{ separator: "__" }` for flatten).

SourceStatus.description:
Readiness ladder for a matrix row's source (#371). A single ordered axis
answering "when does this row run?". Default (when absent) is [`Active`].

[`Active`]: SourceStatus::Active

oneOf.description: Always runs; cannot be narrowed out except by an explicit `--skip <id>`.
Runs by default (bare `faucet run`). The absent-default.
Ready, but opt-in: runs only when requested via `--status available`.
Work-in-progress: runs only under `--status draft`.
Retired, kept for history: runs only under `--status archived`.

CompletenessClaim.description:
"For these column values, this fetch returns *all* the records" (#478).

Declared on the source because a sink sees a page and cannot tell a complete
set from page 1 of 3. The claim alone never deletes anything: `on_missing`
defaults to `ignore`, so acting on it is a separate, explicit opt-in.

scope.description:
The scope this fetch is authoritative for, keyed by **destination**
column names — the `DELETE` runs against destination columns, and a
transform chain may rename fields between source and sink. Values may
carry `${parent.path}` / `${now.*}` tokens, resolved per invocation like
any other config value.

on_missing.description:
What to do about destination rows inside `scope` that this run did not
write. Defaults to `ignore`, so adding a claim can never start deleting
data on its own.

OnMissing.description:
Action for destination rows inside a completeness scope that a run did not
write (#478).

oneOf.description: Leave them alone. The claim is recorded but inert (default).

Delete them — the only way an incremental sync can remove records that
were deleted at the source.

OnBatchErrorSpec.description:
Mirrors `faucet_core::OnBatchError` but with `JsonSchema` derived and
`Deserialize` accepting the YAML/JSON shape. Converted to the core
type during `executor::build_dlq_config`.

QualitySpec.description:
The `quality:` config block. Per-record checks run first (partitioning the
page into survivors + quarantined); per-batch checks then run over the
survivors.

record.description: Per-record checks, evaluated in declared order (first failure wins).

batch.description: Per-batch checks, evaluated per page over the survivors.

RecordCheck.description:
A per-record check. Addressed field accepts the filter/explode path subset
(bare key, `dot.path`, `$['bracketed']`).

Every variant carries `field` (the path to check) and `on_failure` (what a
failure does). Per-record checks accept only [`OnFailure::Quarantine`] or
[`OnFailure::Abort`] — `quarantine_batch` is rejected at compile time
because a per-record failure is always attributable to one row.

oneOf.description: Field present and non-null.

treat_missing_as_null.description:
When `true` (default) a missing field fails; when `false` only an
explicit JSON `null` fails.

on_failure.description: What a failure does: `quarantine` (row to the DLQ) or `abort`.

oneOf.description: Field is a string, non-empty after `trim()`.

field.description:
Path to the checked field. A missing field, a `null`, or a
non-string value all fail.

on_failure.description: What a failure does: `quarantine` (row to the DLQ) or `abort`.

oneOf.description: Field is a string matching `pattern`.

field.description:
Path to the checked field. A missing field or a non-string value
fails.

pattern.description:
Rust `regex`-crate pattern. Unanchored — it only has to match
*somewhere* in the value, so anchor with `^…$` for a full match.
An invalid pattern is rejected at config load, never mid-run.

on_failure.description: What a failure does: `quarantine` (row to the DLQ) or `abort`.

oneOf.description: Field value is a member of `values` (exact JSON equality).

field.description: Path to the checked field. A missing field fails.

values.description:
The allowed values. Must be non-empty. Compared by JSON equality
with no type coercion, so the string `"5"` does not match the
number `5`.

on_failure.description: What a failure does: `quarantine` (row to the DLQ) or `abort`.

oneOf.description: Field value is NOT a member of `values` (exact JSON equality).

field.description:
Path to the checked field. A **missing** field passes — there is no
value to forbid.

values.description:
The forbidden values. Must be non-empty. Compared by JSON equality
with no type coercion.

on_failure.description: What a failure does: `quarantine` (row to the DLQ) or `abort`.

oneOf.description: Field value compares against `value` under `op`.

field.description: Path to the checked field. A missing field fails.

op.description: The comparison to apply, as `field <op> value`.

value.description:
The right-hand side of the comparison. The ordering ops
(`gt`/`gte`/`lt`/`lte`) require a JSON number here — anything else
is rejected at config load — and also require the record's value to
be a number; `eq`/`ne` accept any JSON value.

on_failure.description: What a failure does: `quarantine` (row to the DLQ) or `abort`.

oneOf.description: Field's JSON type equals `expected`.

field.description:
Path to the checked field. A missing field fails, which is distinct
from an `expected: null` match on a present `null`.

on_failure.description: What a failure does: `quarantine` (row to the DLQ) or `abort`.

oneOf.description: Field is a string whose char count is within `[min, max]`.

field.description:
Path to the checked field. A missing field or a non-string value
fails.

min.description:
Inclusive minimum length in Unicode **characters** (not bytes).
Omit for no lower bound.

max.description:
Inclusive maximum length in Unicode **characters** (not bytes).
Omit for no upper bound. At least one of `min`/`max` is required,
and `min <= max`, both enforced at config load.

on_failure.description: What a failure does: `quarantine` (row to the DLQ) or `abort`.

oneOf.description: The whole record validates against a JSON Schema document.

schema.description:
The JSON Schema document, inline. Compiled once at config load —
an invalid schema fails there, not on the first page. The first
validation error becomes the DLQ/abort message.

on_failure.description: What a failure does: `quarantine` (row to the DLQ) or `abort`.

OnFailure.description:
What to do when a check fails. The allowed subset is validated per check
at compile time (see `compile.rs`).

oneOf.description: Route the specific offending row(s) to the DLQ; keep the rest.
Route all survivors of the page to the DLQ; write nothing this page.
Surface `FaucetError::QualityFailure` and fail the run.

CompareOp.description: Ordering / equality operator for the `compare` check.

oneOf.description: Greater than: `field > value`. Both must be JSON numbers.
Greater than or equal: `field >= value`. Both must be JSON numbers.
Less than: `field < value`. Both must be JSON numbers.
Less than or equal: `field <= value`. Both must be JSON numbers.

JSON equality. Two numbers compare by numeric value (`1` == `1.0`, and
large 64-bit integers compare exactly); all other types compare
structurally with no cross-type coercion (string `"5"` != number `5`).

JSON inequality — the negation of [`CompareOp::Eq`] (numbers by value,
other types structurally).

JsonType.description: Expected JSON type for the `type_is` check.

oneOf.description: JSON boolean (`true` / `false`).
JSON number (integer or float).
JSON string.
JSON array.
JSON object.
JSON null. Note: a *missing* field is distinct from an explicit `null`.

BatchCheck.description:
A per-batch check, evaluated per page over the survivors of the per-record
pass.

**Scope is one page, not the whole run** — with a source `batch_size` of
1000, `row_count` sees 1000 rows at a time. Set the source's
`batch_size: 0` to evaluate these over the entire result set instead.

The aggregate checks (`row_count` / `null_rate` / `distinct_count`) cannot
blame an individual row, so they accept only [`OnFailure::Abort`] or
[`OnFailure::QuarantineBatch`]; `unique` *is* row-attributable and so
accepts `quarantine` or `abort`. Either way the wrong choice is rejected at
config load.

oneOf.description: Survivor count is within `[min, max]` (at least one bound required).

min.description:
Inclusive minimum surviving rows in the page. Omit for no lower
bound.

max.description:
Inclusive maximum surviving rows in the page. Omit for no upper
bound. At least one of `min`/`max` is required, and `min <= max`,
both enforced at config load.

on_failure.description:
What a failure does: `abort`, or `quarantine_batch` (every survivor
in the page goes to the DLQ and nothing is written).

oneOf.description: Null-or-missing rate of `field` across survivors is `<= max`.

field.description:
Path to the measured field. A missing field counts the same as an
explicit `null`.

max.description: Maximum allowed null-or-missing proportion, in `[0.0, 1.0]`. Out-of-range values are rejected at compile time.

on_failure.description:
What a failure does: `abort`, or `quarantine_batch` (every survivor
in the page goes to the DLQ and nothing is written).

oneOf.description: The composite `fields` tuple is unique across survivors.

fields.description:
Paths forming the uniqueness key, in order. One path for a simple
key, several for a composite one. Must be non-empty. A missing
field is a distinct key value from an explicit `null`.

on_failure.description:
What a failure does. This check names the offending rows, so
`quarantine` sends the **duplicate occurrences** to the DLQ (the
first occurrence of each key is kept); `abort` fails the run.

oneOf.description: Distinct values of `field` across survivors is within `[min, max]`.

field.description:
Path to the counted field. A missing field counts as its own
distinct value, separate from an explicit `null`.

min.description:
Inclusive minimum number of distinct values. Omit for no lower
bound.

max.description:
Inclusive maximum number of distinct values. Omit for no upper
bound. At least one of `min`/`max` is required, and `min <= max`,
both enforced at config load.

on_failure.description:
What a failure does: `abort`, or `quarantine_batch` (every survivor
in the page goes to the DLQ and nothing is written).

ContractSpec.description:
The `contract:` config block: a declarative, versioned schema + semantic
contract for a pipeline's output, enforced per page after transforms and
quality checks and before the sink write.

version.description:
Contract version, e.g. `"1.0.0"`. Required and non-empty. Carried
into breach errors, DLQ envelopes, and every export format so
producers and consumers can pin the promise they agreed on.
Recommendation: bump the major version on breaking changes (removing
a field, narrowing a type) and the minor version on additive ones.

description.description: Human-readable description of the dataset this contract covers.

owner.description: Owning team or person (documentation metadata; carried into exports).

on_breach.description:
Breach policy: `fail` (default) aborts the run, `quarantine` routes
breaching records to the DLQ (a `dlq:` block is required), `warn`
logs + counts but writes everything.

allow_extra_fields.description:
When `false`, a top-level key not declared in `fields` is a breach
(`extra_field`). Default `true` — additive fields are allowed.

fields.description: The promised top-level fields. Must be non-empty; names must be unique.

OnBreach.description:
What to do when a record breaches the contract. Contract-level (not
per-field): a contract is a single versioned promise, so one policy
governs every rule in it.

oneOf.description:
Surface [`FaucetError::ContractViolation`](crate::FaucetError::ContractViolation)
on the first breach and fail the run (default — a contract is a
promise, so silent divergence is the worst outcome).
Route breaching records to the DLQ; write the rest. Requires a DLQ.
Log + count breaches, but write every record unchanged.

FieldContract.description: One promised top-level field: its type plus optional semantic constraints.

name.description:
Top-level field name (contracts describe the output's top-level shape;
nested objects are typed as `object`).

type.description:
Declared type. `integer` means a JSON number with no fractional part;
`number` accepts any JSON number.

required.description:
When `true` (default) the field must be present in every record.
A non-required field that is absent skips all other checks.

nullable.description:
When `true`, an explicit JSON `null` is allowed (and skips the
type/constraint checks). Default `false`.

enum.description:
Allowed values (exact JSON equality). Must be non-empty when present,
and every value must match the declared `type`. Use `nullable` for
null — `null` is not allowed inside `enum`.

pattern.description: Regex the value must match. `string` fields only.

min_length.description: Minimum string length in characters (inclusive). `string` fields only.

max_length.description: Maximum string length in characters (inclusive). `string` fields only.

description.description: Column description (documentation metadata; carried into exports).

ContractFieldType.description: Declared type of a contract field.

oneOf.description: JSON string.
JSON number with no fractional part (fits `i64`/`u64` as parsed).
Any JSON number (integer or float).
JSON boolean.

JSON object. Nested shapes are treated as one opaque column — a
contract describes the top-level output shape, matching the
schema-drift convention.
JSON array.

MaskingSpec.description:
The `masking:` config block: a declarative, destination-scoped policy that
classifies sensitive fields (by field-name pattern, by value detector, or
by explicit field list) and applies a masking action per page. The masking
pass runs *first* — before the quality, contract, and schema-drift passes
and before every sink write — so PII never reaches a sink, the DLQ, or a
lineage sample unmasked.

Masking never fails a run or quarantines records: every matching field is
rewritten in place. Rules are evaluated in declared order; for a given
field, the first matching rule wins.

description.description: Human-readable description of the policy (documentation metadata).

key.description:
Secret key for keyed hashing/tokenization (`hash` / `tokenize`
actions). When present, masked values are HMAC-SHA256 keyed digests, so
the mapping cannot be reversed by an attacker who lacks the key yet stays
deterministic (equal inputs → equal tokens) so masked values remain
joinable downstream. Pull it from a secrets manager
(`${vault:...}` / `${aws-sm:...}` / …) rather than hard-coding it.

When absent, `hash` / `tokenize` fall back to an *unkeyed* SHA-256
digest — still deterministic, but not secret (anyone can recompute it).

rules.description:
The masking rules. Must be non-empty. Evaluated in declared order; the
first rule that matches a given field wins for that field.

MaskRule.description:
One masking rule: a matcher + the action to apply to matching fields,
optionally scoped to a subset of destination sinks.

name.description:
Optional stable label for this rule — surfaced in logs and as the
`rule` metric label. Defaults to a generated `rule_<n>` when absent.

match.description:
How this rule decides a field is sensitive. At least one of
`field_pattern` / `value_detector` / `fields` must be set.

action.description: What to do with a matching field's value.

applies_to.description:
Destination sinks this rule applies to, by template name (e.g.
`default`, `secure`) or connector kind (e.g. `bigquery`). Empty (the
default) means the rule applies to every sink — so the same source can
be fully masked to one sink and partially masked to another by scoping
rules per destination.

field_pattern.description:
Regex matched against each field's dot-path (e.g. `user.email`,
`contacts.0.phone`). Case-sensitive unless the pattern opts in with
`(?i)`. Name-based classification — cheap and precise when you know
your field names.

value_detector.description:
Value-based PII detector run over each *string* field value.
Conservative (fully anchored) by default to avoid over-masking.

fields.description:
Explicit dot-paths to mask unconditionally — the pre-classification /
tagging escape hatch.

Detector.description:
Built-in value detectors. All are conservative (anchored full-string
matches; the card detector additionally requires a valid Luhn checksum) so
false positives stay rare — masking silently rewrites data, so a
false positive is a data-quality bug, not just noise.

oneOf.description: RFC-5322-ish email address.
13–19 digit card number (spaces/dashes allowed) passing the Luhn check.
US Social Security Number `NNN-NN-NNNN`.
E.164 / North-American phone number.
IPv4 dotted-quad address.

MaskAction.description: What to do with a value once a rule matches it.

oneOf.description:
Replace the value wholesale with a fixed mask (default `"***"`).
Irreversible and not joinable — use for values you never need again.

mask.description:
Replacement value. Defaults to the JSON string `"***"`. Set it to an
explicit `null` to null the field (e.g. for a nullable DB column),
or to any other JSON scalar you prefer.

oneOf.description:
Replace the value with its hex HMAC-SHA256 (keyed) / SHA-256 (unkeyed)
digest. Deterministic → joinable; irreversible.

Replace the value with a short opaque token derived from a keyed digest,
optionally with a stable prefix (e.g. `tok_`). Deterministic → joinable.

prefix.description: Literal prefix prepended to every token (e.g. `"tok_"`).

oneOf.description:
Reveal only the last `keep_last` characters, replacing the rest with
`mask_char` (default `*`). Preserves format/length for readability
(e.g. `****1234`). `keep_last: 0` masks everything.

keep_last.description: Number of trailing characters to keep in the clear. Default `4`.

mask_char.description: Character used for the masked prefix. Default `*`.

on_drift.description: Policy applied when drift is detected.

allow_type_widening.description:
Whether a lossless widening counts as evolvable (vs incompatible).
Only consulted by `evolve`. Default: true.

on_incompatible.description: `evolve` only: action for an incompatible residue. Default: fail.

relax_nullability_on_missing.description:
`evolve` only: whether the **absence** of a destination `NOT NULL`
column from a page may drop that column's `NOT NULL` constraint.

Default `false`: a column merely omitted from one batch is *not*
evidence the column is genuinely optional (a transient/partial page
omits it just as readily as a real schema change), so auto-relaxing
would silently and irreversibly weaken the destination's integrity
(issue #194 / F28). When `false`, an omitted required column is left
untouched — a page that genuinely lacks a required value then fails
loudly at write time rather than degrading the schema. Set `true` only
when you deliberately want missing-column omission to relax the
constraint. Nullability relaxation driven by an *observed* null value
in a present column (a widening that adds `null`) is unaffected by this
flag — that is evidence-based, not omission-based.

OnDrift.description: What to do when drift is detected.

oneOf.description: Detect + emit a metric and a one-shot log; write the page unchanged.
Apply additive/widening DDL to the destination, then write.
Drop unknown (non-destination) fields from every record; write the rest.
Route the records that exhibit the drift to the DLQ; write the rest.
Raise `FaucetError::SchemaDrift` and abort.

OnIncompatible.description:
`evolve`-only: what to do with a narrowing/incompatible change that can't be
auto-applied.

oneOf.description: Abort the run (default).
Route the offending records to the DLQ.

NodeSpec.description:
A single topology node (issue #71). The `kind` discriminator selects the
node type; the remaining fields are kind-specific.

`source` / `sink` nodes pick a template with `ref:` (defaulting to
`default`) and may override `type` / `config` inline — the same shape as a
matrix row's [`PartialConnector`]. `transform` carries a `transforms:`
list. `tee` carries `channel_capacity` + optional `fanout`. `merge` has no
extra fields. `join` carries the hash-join configuration.

oneOf.description: A data source (0 in, 1 out).

config.description: Inline config override (deep-merged onto the resolved template).

oneOf.description: A data sink (1 in, 0 out).

config.description: Inline config override (deep-merged onto the resolved template).

oneOf.description: Transform stages applied per page (1 in, 1 out).
Fan-out: clone each page to every downstream edge (1 in, N out).

channel_capacity.description: Bounded-channel capacity for each outgoing edge.

fanout.description: Optional expected fan-out (outgoing edge count) sanity check.

oneOf.description: Fan-in: forward pages from all inputs in arrival order (N in, 1 out).
Hash-join two upstreams by key (2 in, 1 out).

build.description: The build (right) side — fully buffered as a lookup index.

probe.description: The probe (left) side — streamed and enriched.

project.description: Fields to copy from the matched build record onto the probe record.

on_missing.description: Value used to fill projected fields on a `left`-mode non-match.

JoinMode.description: Join mode — how probe records with no build match are handled.

oneOf.description: Drop probe records that have no matching build record.

Pass probe records through even without a match, filling projected
fields from [`JoinConfig::on_missing`].

JoinSide.description: One side of a [`JoinSpec`]: the incoming edge label plus the dotted key path.

edge.description: Name of the incoming edge (matches an `edges[].as` label).

key.description: Dotted path to the join key inside each record on this side.

Projection.description:
A single field projection: copy `from` (a dotted path into the build
record) onto the probe record under the name `as_`.

from.description: Dotted path inside each build (right) record.

as.description: Output field name written onto the probe (left) record.

OnDuplicate.description: What to do when one probe key matches more than one build record.

oneOf.description: Keep only the first build-side match (deterministic given build order).

Emit one enriched record per build-side match (may duplicate the probe
record).

OnCollision.description:
What to do when a projected `as` name collides with an existing field on
the probe record.

oneOf.description: Overwrite the probe record's field with the projected value.
Leave the probe record's field untouched; skip the projection.
Fail the record with a typed error.

KeyNormalize.description: How to normalize keys before comparison.

oneOf.description: Compare keys as their JSON value (no coercion): `"42"` != `42`.

Coerce scalar keys to their string form before comparison so `"42"`
and `42` match.

as.description: Optional edge label (required on a join's two incoming edges).

id.description:
Row identifier. Required for parent/child references and runtime
`${id.path}` interpolation. Anonymous rows get a synthetic `row-N` id.

parent.description: If set, this row runs once per record produced by the named parent row.

depends_on.description:
Row ids this row waits for. The row starts only after every listed
row (all of its invocations) finishes successfully; a failed or
skipped dependency skips this row. Pure completion-ordering — unlike
`parent:`, no records are consumed and no per-record fan-out occurs.

parent_key.description:
Dotted field path inside each parent record that uniquely identifies
the record. Used as the state-key suffix. Default: `id`.

transforms.description:
Row-level transforms. Appended after `T_pipeline` and `T_source`
(unless `inherit_transforms` is `false` here, in which case both
upstream layers are dropped). `None` or empty list contributes
nothing.

inherit_transforms.description:
When `false`, drops upstream `T_pipeline` and `T_source` transforms
for this row. Default `true`.

dlq.description:
Matrix-row override semantics:
- field absent  → `None`     — inherit from `pipeline.dlq`
- `dlq: null`   → `Some(None)` — disable DLQ for this row
- `dlq: { ... }` → `Some(Some(spec))` — replace base DLQ wholesale

delivery.description: Per-row delivery override. `None` inherits the top-level `delivery`.

tags.description:
Free-form classification tags for this row (#376). Orthogonal to the
source's `status:` readiness ladder — `status` gates whether a row is
eligible; `tags` narrow *within* the eligible set at runtime via
`--tag`. Union-merged with the source template's `tags:` to form the
effective tag set. Validated at expand time (charset
`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$`, deduped).

partition.description:
Split this row into N independent invocations over a chunked range
(#479), each scoped by `${partition.*}` tokens substituted into the
connector configs. Inherits the top-level `partition:` block when unset.

discover.description:
**Discovery dimension** (#501). When set, this row enumerates a value-set
at runtime: it builds `discover.source`, drains it, projects `select`
(JSONPath) from each record, and dedups (first-seen order). The row has
no sink and writes nothing — its value-set is exposed to `for_each` rows
as `${<id>.<as>}`. Runs once per pipeline run, cached across dependents.

for_each.description:
Fan this row out over the **cartesian product** of the named discovery
dimensions (#501) — one invocation per tuple, with `${<dim>.<as>}`
resolved to that tuple's value in the source/sink config. Distinct from
`parent:` (fan-out over one real pipeline's emitted records — a tree, not
a product) and `depends_on:` (completion ordering only). Each id must name
a `discover:` row; the product is bounded by `MAX_MATRIX_PRODUCT`.

weight.description:
Relative cost hint used by `execution.schedule: lpt` (#644) — higher is
dispatched earlier. Ignored under the default `declared` order.

The useful proxy is **bytes moved**, not rows: a 970k-row × 3-column
table is lighter than a 122k-row × 100-column one, so ranking on row
count alone mis-orders wide-but-short objects. `faucet discover` fills
this in from each dataset's estimated rows and column widths; set it by
hand when you know better.

fan_out.description:
**Fan-out axis** (#501), spelled `fan_out:` on the wire. When set, this
row enumerates a value-set at runtime: it builds `fan_out.source`,
drains it, projects `select` (JSONPath) from each record, and dedups
(first-seen order). The row has no sink and writes nothing — its
value-set is exposed to `for_each` rows as `${<id>.<as>}`. Runs once
per pipeline run, cached across dependents.

The historical spelling `discover:` is accepted as an alias (#654 M21).
It collided with the other, unrelated `discover` in the vocabulary —
`Source::discover`, which enumerates a connection's **datasets** — and
the canonical verb for "turn a listed set into one matrix row per
member" is `fan_out` (see the Vocabulary table in
`.claude/rules/architecture.md`).

PartialConnector.description:
A partial connector override carried by a matrix row. Both `type` and
`config` are optional so rows can swap the kind, override only the inner
config, or both. `ref:` (optional) picks which named template under
`pipeline.sources` / `pipeline.sinks` this row instantiates; when absent,
the row inherits the legacy singular `pipeline.source` / `pipeline.sink`
(registered internally as a template named `default`).

ref.description:
Name of the template under `pipeline.sources` / `pipeline.sinks` to
instantiate. `None` falls back to the `default` template.

type.description: Override the connector kind (otherwise inherits from the template).

config.description: Partial config object — deep-merged into the resolved template's config.

status.description:
Per-row readiness override for the source (#371). When `Some`, replaces
the template's `status` (scalar deep-merge). Only meaningful on a row's
`source:` override; a `sink:` override's `status` is ignored.

DeliveryMode.description: Delivery guarantee for a pipeline run.

oneOf.description:
Today's behaviour: a page may be re-delivered after a crash between the
sink write and the bookmark persist. Downstream must tolerate duplicates.

The sink durably records a per-page commit token atomically with the
data; on resume the pipeline skips already-committed pages. Requires a
state store, an idempotent sink, and a deterministic-replay source.

PartitionSpec.description: A partitioned range. `kind` selects the variant.

oneOf.description:
Split an integer range — the shape for an API or table filtered by an id
range (`?id_from=&id_to=`, `WHERE id BETWEEN`).

to.description:
Upper bound, interpreted per `bounds`. Either a literal, or a probe
that discovers it (`{from_source: …, value_path: …}`).

bounds.description:
Whether `to` (and each chunk's `end`) is inclusive or exclusive.

**Required, with no default.** Getting it wrong is silent: half-open
chunks against an inclusive-bound source fetch one record twice per
boundary; inclusive chunks against an exclusive source skip one per
boundary. Neither raises.

to_unbounded.description:
Render the final chunk without an upper bound, so rows appended above
`to` between planning and execution are still read.

Unset defaults to **`true` when `to` is discovered** and `false` when
it is a literal: a probed bound is stale the moment it is read, so the
open tail is what keeps late rows from being missed. An explicit value
always wins, for a range the user knows is closed.

oneOf.description:
Split a time range — the same windowing `faucet backfill` uses, including
its DST-correct calendar steps.

from.description: RFC3339, or a bare date interpreted as midnight in `timezone`.

to.description: Exclusive upper bound; time windows are always half-open.

chunk_size.description:
Window size: `45s`, `30m`, `6h`, `1d`, `1w`, or a bare integer =
seconds. `d`/`w` are calendar steps, so `1d` and `24h` differ across a
DST transition — deliberately.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for date boundaries and calendar steps. Defaults to UTC.

oneOf.description:
Split a countable result set into offset/limit slices — the parallel form
of what a source's serial offset pagination already does.

total.description:
Total rows in the result set. Either a literal, or a probe that
discovers it.

IntBound.description: A discoverable upper bound for an integer range.

anyOf.description: Known up front.

Discovered by running a probe source once — `SELECT MAX(id)`, or a
`?sort=-id&limit=1` request.

BoundProbe.description:
Discover a bound by running a source once and reading one field out of its
first record.

Any source works — the probe is an ordinary connector config, so a SQL
`SELECT MAX(id)`, a REST "last record" request, or anything else the registry
can build. That keeps discovery source-agnostic for the same reason the
substitution is: no connector needs to know this feature exists.

from_source.description: A full source config, `{type, config}`, run once before planning.

value_path.description: JSONPath into the probe's **first** record, e.g. `$.max_id`.

Bounds.description:
Whether a chunk's upper edge is included. See the module docs — this has no
default on purpose.

oneOf.description:
`end` is the last value in the chunk: `[start, end]`. For a source whose
upper-bound filter is inclusive (`id_to=9999` returns 9999).

`end` is the first value *after* the chunk: `[start, end)`. For a source
whose upper-bound filter is exclusive.

CountBound.description: A discoverable row count for an offset range.

max_concurrent.description:
Maximum concurrent pipeline invocations (root + per-parent-record
child invocations all share this budget). Defaults to
`num_cpus::get().min(4)` at runtime when `None`. `0` = **no limit**
(the house `0`-sentinel, like `batch_size: 0`) — every invocation runs
in parallel; before 1.7 a `0` here clamped to fully-serial instead, so
audit any config that relied on that.

on_error.description: What to do when a pipeline invocation fails.

schedule.description:
Order in which ready sibling rows queue for a concurrency permit
(#644). Defaults to `declared` — today's behaviour, byte for byte.

oneOf.description: Skip the failed invocation's subtree but keep running siblings (default).
Cancel every pending and in-flight invocation on first failure.

AdaptiveBatchConfig.description:
Configuration for the adaptive batch-size controller. Lives under
`execution.adaptive_batch_size`. Default `enabled = false` (opt-in); when
disabled the pipeline writes each page exactly as before.

controller.description: Controller algorithm. Only `"aimd"` is implemented in v1.

min.description: Lower bound on the effective batch size.

max.description:
Upper bound. Under within-page reslicing the effective ceiling is
`min(max, page_len)`; values above the source page size are inert.

decrease_factor.description: Multiplicative shrink factor on error / high latency (0 < f < 1).

cooldown_batches.description: Batches to wait after a shrink before allowing growth.

target_latency_ms.description: Optional latency target in ms. `None` = react to errors only.

latency_window.description: Rolling window size for the p50 batch-write latency.

error_threshold.description: Per-batch error rate above which the controller shrinks.

respect_source_max.description:
Never grow the effective batch past the source page size. Only `true`
is supported (the default) — `false` is rejected by [`validate`], since
cross-page buffering would have to hold records across source pages and
break the pipeline's O(batch_size) memory guarantee.

[`validate`]: AdaptiveBatchConfig::validate

log_every.description: Emit a `tracing::info!` summary every N adjustments.

SelectionSpec.description:
Matrix-row selection policy (#377). Currently a single knob:
`include_parents`. Extensible for future selection-model settings.

include_parents.description: How parent/dependency ancestors are resolved for a narrowed run set.

IncludeParents.description:
Policy for pulling a selected row's `parent:` / `depends_on:` ancestors into
the run set when they are not independently selected (#377). The **only**
mechanism that decides ancestor inclusion. Default [`Off`] (strict).

[`Off`]: IncludeParents::Off

oneOf.description:
Include nothing automatically; a required ancestor missing from the run
set is a hard, fail-fast error.

Include required ancestors whose resolved status is eligible; error if a
required ancestor is parked (`available`/`draft`/`archived`).

Include every required ancestor regardless of status (parked ancestors
pulled in too, with a warning); never errors on ancestors.

ObservabilitySpec.description: Top-level observability block: Prometheus scrape endpoint and tracing level.

PrometheusSpec.description: Configuration for the Prometheus metrics HTTP endpoint.

listen.description: Socket address to bind the scrape endpoint on (e.g. `"127.0.0.1:9464"`).

buckets.description:
Custom histogram bucket boundaries. Falls back to the Prometheus default
buckets when `None`.

level.description:
`tracing-subscriber` filter directive (e.g. `"info"`, `"debug"`,
`"faucet=trace"`). Defaults to the value of `RUST_LOG` when `None`.

endpoint.description:
Collector endpoint URL. When empty, defaults to the protocol-specific
localhost address (`http://localhost:4317` for gRPC, `:4318` for HTTP).

headers.description: Extra headers sent on every export request (e.g. backend auth tokens).

sample_ratio.description: Head-based trace sampling ratio, 0.0..=1.0. Default: 1.0 (sample all).

export.description: Which signals to export. Default: `[traces, metrics]`.

metric_interval_secs.description: Metric push interval in seconds. Default: 60.

oneOf.description:
gRPC over tonic (default OTLP port 4317). Must be initialised inside a
tokio runtime.
HTTP/protobuf (default OTLP port 4318).

OtelSignal.description: A telemetry signal that can be exported over OTLP.

retry.description:
Retry/backoff applied to sink-write, flush, and state-store I/O (and
injected into rest/xml/graphql sources).

retry_on.description: Which error classes are retried. Omitted = all four transient classes.

max_attempts.description: Total attempts including the first (1 = no retry).

oneOf.description: No delay between attempts.
Constant `base_ms` delay.
`base_ms * 2^attempt`, capped at `max_ms`.

RetryClass.description:
The transient-failure class an error belongs to. Closed set so it can be a
bounded metric label and a `retry_on` config value.

oneOf.description: HTTP 5xx server error.
HTTP 429 / rate-limit signal.
Connection-level failure (DNS, refused, reset) with no HTTP status.
Request timeout.

consecutive_failures.description: Consecutive exhausted-retry page failures before the circuit opens.

cooldown_secs.description: Re-entry cooldown in seconds (honored by the orchestration layer).

action.description: Terminal action for a persistently failing row.

PoisonActionSpec.description:
Terminal action for a poison row (config spelling of
`faucet_core::PoisonAction`).

oneOf.description: Route to the DLQ (requires a `dlq:` block).
Discard the row.
Propagate the row error and abort the run.

SlaSpec.description:
Declared service-level agreement for a pipeline: freshness and volume
expectations. Violations emit the
`faucet_pipeline_sla_violations_total{pipeline,row,kind}` counter and a
structured warning log; they never fail the run.

max_staleness_secs.description:
Maximum seconds since the last *successful* run before the pipeline
counts as stale. Evaluated when a run fails (against the previous
success) and by `faucet doctor`. Requires a `state:` block to persist
the last-success timestamp.

min_rows_per_run.description:
Static volume floor: a successful run that writes fewer records than
this violates the SLA (catches a source silently returning nothing).
Stateless — works without a `state:` block.

volume_anomaly.description:
Learned-baseline volume anomaly detection over recent successful runs.
Requires a `state:` block to persist the rolling baseline.

VolumeAnomalySpec.description:
How a run's record volume is flagged as anomalous against the rolling
baseline of recent successful runs.

sensitivity.description:
Detection threshold. For `zscore`: the maximum |x − mean| / std
(default 3.0). For `iqr`: the Tukey fence multiplier — a volume outside
[Q1 − k·IQR, Q3 + k·IQR] is anomalous (default 1.5).

min_history.description:
Minimum successful runs of history before detection starts (cold-start
guard). Default 5; must be at least 2.

window.description:
Rolling-window size: how many recent successful-run volumes form the
baseline. Default 20; must be ≥ `min_history`.

oneOf.description: Flag when |volume − mean| / std exceeds `sensitivity`.

Flag when the volume falls outside the Tukey fences
[Q1 − k·IQR, Q3 + k·IQR] with k = `sensitivity`.

ShardingSpec.description: Source-shard distribution settings for clustered (Mode B) execution.

count.description:
Target number of shards to split the source into. Must be `>= 2` (a
count of 1 means "don't shard" — omit the block instead). The actual
shard count may be smaller when the source has fewer natural partitions
(e.g. a key range narrower than `count`).

mode.description: Replication strategy. Only `snapshot_then_cdc` is available in v1.

snapshot.description: One-time bulk-read source used to back-fill the destination before CDC.

continuous.description:
After the snapshot completes, keep streaming CDC until SIGTERM/SIGINT.
When `false`, drain CDC once and exit (useful for tests / batch runs).

oneOf.description:
Capture the CDC position, bulk-snapshot the table, then stream CDC from
that position. Pair with `write_mode: upsert` for a true mirror.

SnapshotSpec.description: The one-time snapshot source (a non-CDC bulk reader of the same upstream DB).

source.description: Bulk-read source connector (e.g. `postgres` running `SELECT * FROM t`).

window.description:
Default window chunk when `--window` is not passed — a duration like
`1d`, `6h`, `30m`, `45s`, or `1w`. Omitted = the whole range runs as a
single unit.

concurrency.description:
Default max concurrently-running window units when `--concurrency` is
not passed. Defaults to 1 (sequential).

timezone.description:
IANA timezone (e.g. `America/New_York`) in which date boundaries like
`--from 2026-06-01` are interpreted and `${now.*}` tokens render.
Defaults to UTC.

ScheduleSpec.description:
Top-level `schedule:` block. Presence of this block is what makes a config
runnable by `faucet schedule`.

cron.description:
Cron expression. 5-field standard Unix cron (`minute hour day-of-month
month day-of-week`), or 6-field with a leading seconds field for
sub-minute schedules.

overlap_policy.description: What to do when a tick fires while the previous run is still in flight.

max_runs.description: Stop cleanly after this many *successful* runs. `None` = run forever.

max_consecutive_failures.description:
Exit non-zero after this many *consecutive* failed runs (so a supervisor
restarts / pages). A success resets the counter. `None` = never exit on
failure (alert via the `consecutive_failures` gauge instead).

start_immediately.description: Run once on startup before waiting for the first scheduled tick.

run_timeout_secs.description:
Optional per-run kill switch (seconds). A run exceeding this is aborted
and counts as a failed run.

shutdown_grace_secs.description:
On SIGTERM/SIGINT, await the in-flight run this many seconds before
aborting it. Default 30 (matches Kubernetes' default termination grace).

OverlapPolicy.description: Behaviour when a tick fires while a run is still in progress.

oneOf.description: Drop the overlapping tick (default).
Buffer one missed tick and run it when the current run finishes.
Treat an overlap as fatal — exit non-zero.
Log the failure and wait for the next tick (default).
Exit non-zero on the first failed run.

namespace.description: OpenLineage namespace for the emitted job/datasets.

job_name.description:
Job-name template. `${name}` / `${row_id}` / `${now.*}` are resolved
per matrix row at run time.

include_column_lineage.description: Emit column-level lineage facets where the transform chain is mappable.

include_schema_facet.description: Emit dataset schema facets (inferred from a record sample).

include_source_code_facet.description:
Emit the resolved config body as a SourceCode facet. Off by default —
the resolved config may contain secrets; enabling warns.

sample_records.description: Max records sampled for schema/column facets. Default 100.

heartbeat_interval.description: RUNNING heartbeat interval. Default 30s; only used when `emit_on.running`.

Transport.description:
Lineage event transport.

Uses the project-wide `{ type, config: { … } }` shape (adjacently tagged),
matching connectors and the shared auth catalog. `deny_unknown_fields` is
intentionally omitted — serde does not honor it on tagged enums (same as
`faucet-core` auth, websocket, grpc).

oneOf.description: POST each event to an OpenLineage HTTP endpoint (e.g. Marquez).
Append each event as one JSON line to a local file.
Produce each event as a JSON message to a Kafka topic.

HttpAuth.description:
HTTP transport auth. Same `{ type, config: { … } }` shape as connector auth
(e.g. `{ type: bearer, config: { token: … } }`).

CatalogSpec.description:
The top-level `catalog:` block: opts a `faucet run` / `schedule` /
`replicate` pipeline into recording the Data Movement Catalog after every
successful root invocation. `faucet serve` records into its `--history`
backend automatically — this block is for the non-serve runtimes (and for
`faucet catalog`, which reads the same store).

url.description:
Where the catalog is stored: `sqlite:<path>` (e.g.
`sqlite:./faucet-catalog.db`), a `postgres://…` URL, or `memory`
(process-lifetime only — useful for tests). SQL backends require the
matching `serve-history-sqlite` / `serve-history-postgres` build
feature. Point `faucet serve --history` at the same URL to browse the
accumulated catalog in the control plane + web console.

sample_records.description:
How many records to sample per run for schema inference (per side).
The sample bounds memory; the schema timeline only ever stores the
inferred schema, never the records.

name.description:
Stable, human-readable name. Used in metric labels, dedupe keys, and
log lines — keep it unique across rules.

on.description: Event kinds this rule fires on. **Empty = every kind.**

min_severity.description:
Only deliver events at or above this severity. Defaults to `info`
(deliver everything the `on` selector matches).

dedupe_window_secs.description:
Coalesce repeated identical events (same rule + dedupe key) within this
many seconds — leading-edge: the first event fires, subsequent ones
inside the window are dropped as `coalesced`. Absent / `0` disables
coalescing.

dlq_threshold.description:
For the `dlq_threshold` event only: fire when a run routed **at least**
this many rows to the DLQ. Defaults to `1` (any DLQ traffic).

EventKind.description: The lifecycle / health events a rule can subscribe to.

oneOf.description: A pipeline run (or its final flush) failed.
A pipeline run completed successfully.
A post-run SLA check was violated (staleness / min_rows / volume).
The resilience circuit breaker tripped open.
A data contract breach aborted the run (`on_breach: fail`).

A run routed rows to the dead-letter queue at/over the configured
threshold.

The cron scheduler appears stuck (no heartbeat / consecutive-failure
exit). Emitted by `faucet schedule`.

Severity.description:
Event severity — ordered so `min_severity` can gate with `>=`. A rule with
no `min_severity` defaults to the lowest floor (`info`), so it delivers
everything it subscribes to.

oneOf.description: Informational (e.g. `run_success`).
A degraded but non-failing condition (e.g. `sla_breach`, `dlq_threshold`).
A failure that stopped the run (e.g. `run_failure`, `contract_abort`).

A systemic failure needing immediate attention (e.g. `circuit_open`,
`scheduler_stuck`).

ChannelSpec.description:
A delivery channel. Adjacently tagged `{ type, config }` to match the
project-wide connector / auth / lineage-transport shape.

oneOf.description: Slack incoming webhook.
PagerDuty Events API v2 (trigger + auto-resolve).
Generic HTTP POST with an optional HMAC-SHA256 signature.

webhook_url.description:
Incoming-webhook URL. Supply via `${env:...}` / `${secret:...}` so it is
redacted from logs.

source.description:
Optional `source` field for the PD payload (defaults to the pipeline
name).

endpoint.description:
Override the events endpoint (tests / EU service region). Defaults to
the global US endpoint.

headers.description: Extra headers sent with every request.

hmac_secret.description:
If set, sign the JSON body with HMAC-SHA256 and send the lowercase-hex
digest in `signature_header`. Supply via `${env:...}` / `${secret:...}`.

extra_fields.description:
Static fields merged into the emitted JSON body (#480), so a callback can
be tagged with a tenant, environment, or external job id. Values go
through the normal interpolation pass, so `${env:...}` / `${vars.X}` /
`${secret:...}` all work.

Keys that collide with a field faucet itself emits (`event`, `severity`,
`pipeline`, `row`, `title`, `message`, `details`, `run_id`,
`invocation_id`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `duration_secs`) are

oneOf.description:
Fetch a token from an arbitrary HTTP endpoint.

The endpoint is called, the token is extracted from the JSON response
using `token_path` (a JSONPath expression), and then used as a Bearer
token (or in a custom header if `header_name` is set).

Tokens are cached and refreshed automatically when `expiry_path`
is provided and the server returns an expiry value.

method.description: HTTP method for the token request (e.g. GET, POST).

body.description: Optional JSON body for the token request.

token_path.description: JSONPath expression to extract the token string from the response.

expiry_path.description:
Optional JSONPath expression to extract the expiry (in seconds)
from the response. When absent, the token is cached indefinitely.

Must be in `(0.0, 1.0]`. Defaults to `0.9`.

(`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, required by RFC-6749 OAuth
token endpoints like Salesforce/Google).

A `{ ref: <name> }` pointer to a named provider in the top-level `auth:`
catalog. The only permitted key is `ref`.

oneOf.description:
POST-search pagination: the next-page cursor is read from the response
body via `next_token_path` and written **into the request JSON body** at
`body_cursor_field` for the next request (rather than a query param).

The first request uses `config.body` unchanged; each subsequent request
sets `body[body_cursor_field] = <extracted cursor>`. Pagination stops when
`next_token_path` is null/absent, and a repeated cursor trips the same
loop guard as [`PaginationStyle::Cursor`]. Used by e.g. HubSpot CRM
`POST /crm/v3/objects/{obj}/search` (`$.paging.next.after` → `after`).

The full URL of the next page is embedded in the response body.
`next_link_path` is a JSONPath expression pointing to that URL field
(e.g. `"$.next_link"`).  Pagination stops when the field is absent,
null, or an empty string.

Offset/limit pagination that writes the offset and limit into the JSON
**request body** (POST-query APIs), rather than the query string
([`Offset`](Self::Offset)) or a cursor token
([`CursorInBody`](Self::CursorInBody)). Each request sends
`body[offset_field] = <offset>` and `body[limit_field] = <limit>`; the
offset advances by the page's record count. With `stop_when_short`
(default `true`) a page shorter than `limit` ends pagination; a zero-record
page always ends it, and a repeated identical page trips a loop guard.

Keyset pagination by the running max/min of a record field (#554). After
each page the aggregate of `field` over its records is injected into the
next request (as a query param or body field per `into`) at `param`. With
`stop_when_short` (default `true`) a page shorter than `page_size` ends
pagination; a zero-record page always ends it, and a non-advancing cursor
trips a loop guard.

field.description: Record field whose value drives the cursor.

into.description: Where the cursor is injected on the next request (default `query`).

param.description: Request parameter/body-field name the cursor is written to.

stop_when_short.description: Stop when a page returns fewer than `page_size` records (default `true`).

page_size.description: Expected page size, used for the short-page stop check.

source_xml__SoapConfig.description:
First-class SOAP ergonomics for the XML source.

This is **sugar** over the existing XML-over-HTTP request/response path —
not a WSDL client. When present, the source assembles a SOAP envelope for
the request body, injects the version-appropriate headers, and (by default)
resolves [`XmlStreamConfig::records_element_path`] relative to
`Envelope.Body` and surfaces SOAP `<Fault>` responses as errors.

action.description:
The SOAP action. For 1.1 it becomes the `SOAPAction` header; for 1.2 it
is carried as the `action` parameter of the `Content-Type` header.
Optional — omit for actionless operations.

body_inner.description:
The XML fragment placed inside `<soap:Body>` — typically the operation
element, e.g. `<GetUsers xmlns="urn:example"/>`. Mutually exclusive with
the top-level [`XmlStreamConfig::body`].

namespaces.description:
Extra namespace declarations (prefix → URI) added to the envelope
element. The `soap` prefix is reserved for the envelope namespace and
any entry using it is ignored.

path_relative_to_body.description:
When `true` (default), [`XmlStreamConfig::records_element_path`] is
resolved relative to `Envelope.Body` — i.e. `Envelope.Body.` is
auto-prepended, so you write `GetUsersResponse.Users.User`. Set `false`
to supply the fully-qualified path from the document root.

fault_as_error.description:
When `true` (default), a SOAP `<Fault>` in the response raises
[`FaucetError::Source`]. When `false`,
a fault yields zero records (logged once).

source_xml__SoapVersion.description:
SOAP protocol version. Controls the envelope namespace and the HTTP
header shape used to carry the SOAP action.

Deserializes from the wire strings `"1.1"` / `"1.2"`.

oneOf.description:
SOAP 1.1 — envelope namespace `http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/`,
action carried in a separate `SOAPAction` header.

SOAP 1.2 — envelope namespace `http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope`,
action carried as a `Content-Type` parameter (no `SOAPAction` header).
Page-number pagination with a query parameter.

each subsequent request replace the request body with `next_body` (with

repeats (loop guard), honouring `max_pages`. For stateful XML/SOAP APIs

source_postgres__ShardConfig.description:
Primary-key range sharding settings for the PostgreSQL source.

The source is split by contiguous ranges of an **integer-typed** column:
each shard runs `SELECT * FROM (<query>) WHERE <key> >= lo AND <key> < hi`.
The column must be present in the query's output and orderable as a 64-bit
integer (e.g. a `bigint`/`int`/`serial` primary key).

**Nullable keys:** if the key column contains NULLs, those rows are not
visible to the `MIN`/`MAX` range enumeration. They are still read — exactly
one shard (the last) additionally matches `<key> IS NULL`, so NULL-key rows
are covered by precisely one shard with no loss and no duplication.

key.description:
Integer column to range-partition on. Quoted as an identifier before use,
so it is safe against injection but must name a real output column.

source_postgres-cdc__SlotType.description: Lifetime of a newly-created replication slot.

oneOf.description: Survives disconnect; pins WAL until consumed or dropped. Default.

source_postgres-cdc__CdcTls.description: TLS configuration for the CDC replication connection.

oneOf.description: No TLS — plaintext (default, back-compatible).
Require TLS but do not verify the server certificate.

system roots when `None`).
Require TLS and verify both the certificate chain and the hostname.

source_mysql__ShardConfig.description:
Primary-key range sharding settings for the MySQL source.

The source is split by contiguous ranges of an **integer-typed** column:
each shard runs ``SELECT * FROM (<query>) WHERE `key` >= lo AND `key` < hi``.
The column must be present in the query's output and orderable as a 64-bit
integer (e.g. a `BIGINT`/`INT` auto-increment primary key).

**Nullable keys:** if the key column contains NULLs, those rows are not
visible to the `MIN`/`MAX` range enumeration. They are still read — exactly
one shard (the last) additionally matches ``` `key` IS NULL ```, so NULL-key
rows are covered by precisely one shard with no loss and no duplication.

key.description:
Integer column to range-partition on. Quoted as an identifier (backticks)
before use, so it is safe against injection but must name a real output
column.

Require encryption; fail if the server does not offer it. Maps to

No transport encryption. Maps to `EncryptionLevel::NotSupported`.

source_mssql__MssqlReplication.description:
How the source replicates rows across runs.

Serializes as `{ type: full }` or
`{ type: incremental, column: "...", initial_value: ... }`.

oneOf.description: Every run fetches the full result set (default).

Only rows whose `column` is strictly greater than the stored bookmark
(or `initial_value` on the first run) are emitted.

The bookmark is applied two ways: if the query contains the literal
token `@bookmark`, it is bound as a parameter so the server filters
(efficient); the source *also* filters client-side as a correctness
backstop. The new maximum of `column` is persisted on the final page.

column.description: Column whose value is the replication cursor (e.g. `updated_at`).

initial_value.description: Lower bound used on the first run, before any bookmark is stored.

source_mssql__ShardConfig.description:
Primary-key range sharding settings for the MSSQL source.

The source is split by contiguous ranges of an **integer-typed** column:
each shard runs `SELECT * FROM (<query>) WHERE [key] >= lo AND [key] < hi`.
The column must be present in the query's output and orderable as a 64-bit
integer (e.g. a `BIGINT`/`INT` `IDENTITY` primary key).

**`ORDER BY`:** T-SQL forbids `ORDER BY` inside a derived table (without
`TOP`/`OFFSET`), so a sharded query must not end in a top-level `ORDER BY`
— ordering across concurrently-executing shards is meaningless anyway.

**Nullable keys:** if the key column contains NULLs, those rows are not
visible to the `MIN`/`MAX` range enumeration. They are still read — exactly
one shard (the last) additionally matches `[key] IS NULL`, so NULL-key rows
are covered by precisely one shard with no loss and no duplication.

key.description:
Integer column to range-partition on. Quoted as an identifier (brackets)
before use, so it is safe against injection but must name a real output
column.

source_sqlite__ShardConfig.description:
Primary-key range sharding settings for the SQLite source.

The source is split by contiguous ranges of an **integer-typed** column:
each shard runs `SELECT * FROM (<query>) WHERE "key" >= lo AND "key" < hi`.
The column must be present in the query's output and orderable as a 64-bit
integer (e.g. an `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` rowid alias).

**Nullable keys:** if the key column contains NULLs, those rows are not
visible to the `MIN`/`MAX` range enumeration. They are still read — exactly
one shard (the last) additionally matches `"key" IS NULL`, so NULL-key rows
are covered by precisely one shard with no loss and no duplication.

key.description:

so it is safe against injection but must name a real output column.

path.description:
URL path, relative to `base_url`. May contain `{key}` placeholders that
are substituted per-partition (e.g. `"/orgs/{org_id}/users"`).

auth.description:
Authentication: either inline (`{ type, config }`) or a `{ ref: <name> }`
pointer to a shared provider in the CLI's top-level `auth:` catalog.

headers.description:
Static request headers sent on **every** request (data pages, async-job
submit/poll/fetch requests, and OData `$metadata` discovery probes).
Applied *before* the auth provider's header placements, so an auth
header of the same name always wins on a clash. Values honor
`${env:}` / `${param.*}` load-time interpolation and pass through the
secrets/redaction boundary like other config strings. Invalid header
names/values are rejected at config load
([`FaucetError::Config`](faucet_core::FaucetError::Config)), never a
mid-run panic.

```yaml
headers:
  Prefer: transient
  Accept: application/json
```

query_params.description:
Static query-string parameters, rendered as `?k=v`. Values honor
`{placeholder}` context substitution for child sources. Empty by
default.

The `#[serde(default)]` here is load-bearing: without it this field was
**required**, so any config omitting it failed to deserialize — while
its siblings `headers` and `query_params_multi` both defaulted. Several
shipped examples omitted it and could not run at all, which nothing
caught because `faucet validate` did not deserialize connector configs
until #609.

query_params_multi.description:
Repeated / array-valued query params (#536), rendered as repeated keys —
e.g. `{ "group_by[]": ["api_key_id", "model"] }` → `?group_by[]=api_key_id&group_by[]=model`.
Applied alongside (in addition to) [`query_params`](Self::query_params);
use this for APIs that need a key to appear more than once (`group_by[]`,
repeated `expand`/`fields`). Values honor `{placeholder}` context
substitution for child sources, like `query_params`. Empty by default.

max_retries.description:
Number of retries (after the first attempt) for transient request
failures. Default `3`.

**Precedence note:** the REST source predates the unified pipeline
`resilience:` policy. When this field (or [`retry_backoff`](Self::retry_backoff))
is left at its default, an injected `RetryPolicy` (e.g. from a
pipeline-level `resilience:` block, via
[`RestStream::with_retry_policy`](crate::RestStream::with_retry_policy))
governs the retry budget. Setting this field away from its default makes
it win — an explicit per-connector value is never silently overridden by
a pipeline-wide default.

retry_backoff.description:
Base exponential-backoff delay between retries. Default `1s`. Shares the
legacy-field precedence rule documented on [`max_retries`](Self::max_retries).

tolerated_http_errors.description:
HTTP status codes that should **not** cause an error. Responses with
these codes are treated as empty pages (no records, no further pages).

replication_key.description: Field name (not a JSONPath) used for incremental replication bookmarking.

start_replication_value.description:
Bookmark value: records where `record[replication_key] <= start_replication_value`
are filtered out when `replication_method` is `Incremental`.

state_key.description:
Opt-in identifier used by [`Pipeline::with_state_store`](faucet_core::Pipeline::with_state_store)
to persist this stream's bookmark across runs. When set, the pipeline
will load any previously-stored bookmark before fetching and write the
new bookmark only after the sink confirms the batch.

Keys must satisfy [`faucet_core::state::validate_state_key`].

name.description: Human-readable stream name (used in logging and Singer SCHEMA messages).

primary_keys.description: Field names that uniquely identify a record (Singer `key_properties`).

schema.description: JSON Schema describing the structure of each record.

schema_sample_size.description:
Maximum number of records to sample when inferring the schema via
[`crate::stream::RestStream::infer_schema`].  `0` means sample all
available records (up to `max_pages`).  Defaults to `100`.

partitions.description:
Each entry is a context map whose values are substituted into `path`
placeholders. The stream is executed once per partition and results are
concatenated.  Empty means run once with no substitution.

partition_concurrency.description:
Maximum number of partitions to fetch concurrently.
`None` means sequential processing (backward compatible default).

tls.description:
Optional client-certificate (mutual TLS) config. When set, the source
presents a client certificate on **every** request — data requests and
any inline auth token request (both go through the same HTTP client).
Requires the crate's `mtls` feature; a `tls` block on a build without it
is a load-time error rather than being silently ignored.

response_format.description:
How to parse the response body. `json` (default) uses JSONPath
extraction (`records_path`); `csv` / `excel` parse a tabular **file**
body into records — for authenticated file endpoints such as a Microsoft
Graph / OneDrive / SharePoint `…/content` download or any signed export
URL. In file mode a single response is fetched (pagination must be
`none`) and `records_path` does not apply. `excel` requires the crate's
`excel` feature.

csv_delimiter.description:
CSV field delimiter byte (default `,`). Used only when
`response_format: csv`.

csv_has_headers.description:
Whether the first CSV row is a header row supplying field names
(default `true`). When `false`, fields are named `column_0`, `column_1`, …

excel_sheet.description:
Excel worksheet to read: a sheet name, or a 0-based index as a string.
When omitted, the first worksheet is used. `response_format: excel` only.

excel_header_row.description:
0-based index of the Excel header row (default `0`). Rows above it are
skipped; the header row supplies field names. `response_format: excel` only.

replication_bind.description:
Bind the stored bookmark into the outgoing request (query param / header /
body field / path) so the server returns only new rows. Composes with the
existing `replication_key` client-side filter, which stays active as a
safety net. Requires `replication_method: incremental` + `replication_key`.

odata.description:
Speak the OData protocol: `@odata.nextLink` paging, the `$.value`
envelope, `$select`/`$filter`/`$expand`/`$orderby` sugar, and
`$metadata` (EDMX) → schema discovery. When set, it derives the
pagination, `records_path`, query params, and `Prefer` header at load
time (explicit values still win). See [`ODataConfig`].

drop_key_prefixes.description:
Drop per-record keys starting with any of these prefixes (#654 M24).

Protocol control fields — OData's `@odata.etag` / `@odata.editLink`,
JSON:API's `links`, HAL's `_links` — are metadata, not data, and are
often invalid column names downstream. An `odata:` block implies
`@odata.` (the prefix that used to be hardcoded), so existing configs
need no change; list prefixes here for any other protocol envelope.

decode.description:
Decode the response body before record extraction: a chain of
`extract` (JSONPath) / `base64` / `gunzip` / `unzip` / `parse`
(json|csv|xlsx|xml) steps. Lets a source consume base64/compressed/file
payloads (e.g. a base64 XLSX inside a SOAP body, or a gzipped-CSV export).
When set, it replaces the `response_format` body parsing, and pagination
must be `none`. See [`DecodeStep`](crate::decode::DecodeStep).

async_job.description:
Run a submit→poll→fetch job lifecycle instead of a single GET, for
bulk/export/report-run APIs (Salesforce Bulk, Stripe Reporting, …). The
fetched result flows through `decode:` / `response_format`. When set,
pagination must be `none`. See [`AsyncJobConfig`](crate::async_job::AsyncJobConfig).

window.description:
Bound each request to a rolling `[start, end)` window between the stored
bookmark and `now`, iterating the windows within one run (each `step`
wide) with per-window bookmark durability. For APIs that require — or cap —
a bounded date range (analytics/ads/reporting feeds). Parity with Airbyte's
`DatetimeBasedCursor`. Requires `replication_method: incremental` +
`replication_key`, and a start bookmark (from state, or
`start_replication_value`). See [`WindowSpec`](faucet_core::WindowSpec).

record_ancestors.description:
When `records_path` selects a **nested** array element (e.g.
`$.data[*].data.object`), copy fields from the enclosing `[*]`
array-element ancestor onto each emitted record. The map is
`dest_field: ancestor_relative_path` — for each matched leaf, the source
walks up to the array-element ancestor and copies the named path onto the
record under `dest_field`. Absent ⇒ records are emitted unchanged.

```yaml
records_path: "$.data[*].data.object"
record_ancestors: { event_id: "id", event_created: "created" }
```

Requires `records_path` to contain an array wildcard `[*]`; mutually
exclusive with [`records_multi`](Self::records_multi).

records_multi.description:
Emit several record arrays from one response in a single page (sharing one
pagination advance), each stamped with a user-defined op marker under
[`op_field`](Self::op_field). Composes with a downstream
`write_mode: upsert` + `delete_marker` so added/modified/removed feeds
route correctly. Mutually exclusive with `records_path` /
`record_ancestors`, and requires `response_format: json` with no
`decode:` pipeline.

```yaml
records_multi:
  - { path: "$.added[*]",    op: upsert }
  - { path: "$.modified[*]", op: upsert }
  - { path: "$.removed[*]",  op: delete }
op_field: _op
```

op_field.description:
Field name each [`records_multi`](Self::records_multi) record is stamped
with its spec's `op` value. Defaults to `_op` when omitted.

persist_cursor.description:
Persist the terminal pagination cursor as this run's bookmark (riding the
existing `StreamPage.bookmark` / `StateStore` path — no core trait change)
and, on resume, seed the stored bookmark back into the first request
(query param for `cursor`, request body field for `cursor_in_body`) before
paging. Only meaningful with `pagination: cursor` / `cursor_in_body`;
mutually exclusive with `window` slicing. Default `false`.

discovery.description:
Generic, vendor-neutral discovery recipe: declare which API calls to make
and how to extract datasets from their JSON responses (reusing this
source's `auth` / `base_url` / `headers`). Powers `faucet discover` and
run-time fan-out for any REST API with a listing / describe shape, with no
connector-specific code. See [`DiscoverySpec`](crate::discovery::DiscoverySpec).

anyOf.title: RestStreamConfig
anyOf.description:
Configuration for a RestStream.

`#[serde(default)]` at the container level: every field falls back to its
value from the [`Default`] impl below when omitted. Without it, **22 fields
were required** — a config had to spell out `max_retries`, `retry_backoff`,
`tolerated_http_errors`, `primary_keys`, `partitions`,
`schema_sample_size` and more before it would deserialize at all. That is
why the shipped examples are so verbose, and several of them still omitted
one field and could not run; nothing caught it because `faucet validate`
did not deserialize connector configs until #609.

`base_url` stays required — in serde *and* in the generated JSON Schema, so
`faucet init` still marks it `# REQUIRED`. Everything else defaults to the
value in the [`Default`] impl below.

`batch_size = 0` is the "no batching" sentinel: the page-size variable

upstream schema requires a non-null `first:` argument this will

(e.g. `"Envelope.Body.GetUsersResponse.Users.User"`).
